newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen weaker as bonds slump on durables.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen weaker as bonds slump on durables.

text.p: U.S. stocks are poised to open lower on Friday as bonds fell sharply after September U.S. durable goods orders were far stronger than expected.
New orders for durable goods rose 4.6 percent, the largest increase in nearly four years, to a seasonally adjusted $174.1 billion after declining a revised 3.5 percent decline in August.
The long bond slumped 13/32, boosting its yield to 6.88 percent. December S&P 500 index futures lost 1.85 to 701.95, indicating the Dow industrials might fall about 15 points.

Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp, "It's a very big number but it's important to keep two things in mind: It's a September number and it's a very, very volatile and unpredictable number."
